definition.title: Planetary System Builder
learning_objectives: Relate stellar and planetary mass plus semimajor axis to an ideal Keplerian orbital period.
Compare multiple circular non-interacting planet orbits around one synthetic star.
Interpret a published conservative habitable-zone reference without equating that band with habitability.
Use adjacent mutual-Hill spacing as a limited pairwise circular-orbit diagnostic without claiming long-term multi-planet stability.

fields.name: planets
fields.meaning: One through eight explicitly ordered planet records. Each planet supplies nominal terrestrial mass and semimajor axis.
fields.valid_range: 1 <= planet_count <= 8; 0.01 <= mass_mearth <= 320; 0.01 <= semi_major_axis_au <= 20; semimajor axes strictly increase

input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject booleans, non-finite values, out-of-range values, non-tuples, planet counts outside 1..8, non-planet records, non-increasing semimajor axes, and total planet-to-star mass-parameter ratio above 0.1. No scientific input is silently sorted, clamped, deduplicated, or normalized.

output_schema: Kopparapu 2014 1-Earth-mass conservative runaway-greenhouse inner and maximum-greenhouse outer reference edges
per-planet exact two-body Keplerian orbital period using nominal mass parameters
per-planet placement relative to the reference HZ band
adjacent-pair mutual Hill radius, separation in mutual Hill radii, and pairwise warning context
explicit stellar-consistency, habitability, and long-term-stability caveats

equations.kepler_period: T^2 = 4*pi^2*a^3/[G*(Mstar+Mplanet)]; implemented using exact adopted nominal mass parameters so G does not need to be separately multiplied into nominal masses
equations.hz_effective_flux: S_eff = S_eff_sun + a*Tstar + b*Tstar^2 + c*Tstar^3 + d*Tstar^4, where Tstar = Teff - 5780 K
equations.two_planet_reference: For two initially circular planets, Delta > 2*sqrt(3) is the cited analytic Hill-stability criterion; Builder v1 uses the threshold only as pairwise context.

definition.sampling_policy: Builder v1 returns one deterministic record per submitted planet and one deterministic mutual-Hill record per adjacent pair. It performs no time integration and generates no n-body trajectory.
definition.default_preset: Synthetic 1 nominal-Solar-mass, 1 nominal-Solar-luminosity, 5780 K star with three 1-Earth-mass planets at 0.7, 1.0, and 2.0 AU. This preset is deliberately illustrative and is not the Solar System or an observed exoplanet system.
assumptions: All planet orbits are circular, coplanar, and non-interacting.
Each planet's period is calculated as an isolated two-body star-plus-planet orbit.
Stellar mass, luminosity, and effective temperature are independent educational inputs rather than a fitted stellar-evolution state.
The habitable-zone band is the Kopparapu et al. 2014 1-Earth-mass conservative main-sequence climate-model reference.
The mutual-Hill diagnostic is evaluated only for adjacent pairs ordered by submitted semimajor axis.
A pair above the cited two-circular-planet threshold receives no pairwise Hill warning, but this does not establish long-term or whole-system stability.
limitations: No n-body integration, mutual perturbations, eccentricity, inclination, orbital phase, apsidal precession, secular evolution, migration, tides, scattering, collisions, ejections, or relativistic corrections.
No resonance identification or resonance-stability analysis.
No stellar-evolution consistency solver; allowed stellar mass, luminosity, and effective-temperature values are independent pedagogical controls.
The HZ model is a one-dimensional climate-model reference for main-sequence stars in the source-published 2600-7200 K temperature interval.
Habitable-zone placement does not establish an atmosphere, liquid surface water, habitability, biosignatures, or life.
The pairwise mutual-Hill threshold is not a long-term multi-planet stability guarantee and does not replace numerical dynamical integration.
No observed-system fitting, planet mass-radius relation, composition inference, atmosphere model, or uncertainty propagation.

sources.title: Keplerian Orbits and Dynamics of Exoplanets
sources.organization_or_authors: Carl D. Murray and Alexandre C. M. Correia

validation_fixtures.purpose: At Teff=5780 K and L=1 Lsun, the 1-Earth-mass conservative source coefficients reproduce approximately 0.950443 AU runaway-greenhouse and 1.676004 AU maximum-greenhouse edges.
A 1 nominal-Earth-mass planet at 1 AU around a 1 nominal-Solar-mass star has the deterministic exact-nominal-parameter period used by the model.
The 2600 K and 7200 K source-domain endpoints produce finite positive ordered HZ edges.
Planets interior to, exactly within, and exterior to the returned reference band serialize the explicit three-state placement taxonomy.
Adjacent-pair R_H and Delta reproduce the cited Fabrycky formula using nominal mass-parameter ratios.
An adjacent circular pair at or below Delta=2*sqrt(3) emits pairwise_close_warning without a whole-system instability claim.
An adjacent pair above the reference threshold emits no_pairwise_hill_warning while preserving the explicit no-stability-guarantee explanation.
A valid one-planet system returns no adjacent-pair diagnostics.
Equal or descending submitted semimajor axes are rejected rather than silently sorted.
Identical canonical inputs produce exactly identical immutable results.
Bool, non-finite, out-of-range, count, and total planet-to-star mass-ratio violations fail closed.
Source, constant, coefficient, preset, fixture, and model-version drift is rejected by the strict artifact loader.

scientific_validation.method: Cross-check the exact two-body period relation using IAU nominal mass parameters and AU; reproduce the published Kopparapu 1-Earth-mass conservative source coefficients and temperature boundaries; reproduce Fabrycky mutual-Hill definitions and pairwise threshold while testing that no whole-system stability verdict is emitted.

tools.name: pytest
tools.role: Analytic source-reference, boundary, property, deterministic, domain, and artifact-integrity regression tests.
